description: Claude Code from its native Windows installer: its binary on disk, and the same binary running.
why: The Windows home root (SPEC.md 6.4.7) against real rows: the file and the process both come back as C:\Users\<user>\.local\bin\claude.exe, and `~/.local/bin/claude` cannot match an `.exe` -- home-prefix refuses a name that only starts with a value, which is what keeps claude-monitor from reading as Claude Code -- so each is a value of its own. The proc row is what marks the finding running. `forbid` keeps Claude Desktop, a different product from the same vendor, from being claimed by Claude Code's rows.
known_gaps: The installer may also create ~\.claude, which names the agent too, so must_find alone would pass with either new value wrong. require_rows pins both rows, and the coverage gate holds each value to a row it matched.
A launch through an 8.3 short path keeps the short name in processes.path, which no value matches. Nothing here launches one.
